correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northern opening and headward feeder
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is north of the state boundary. Ensenada’s southern Relieve map depicts the southward drainage east of the separately labeled Purificación corridor and its approach to the boundary. It supplies the correct headward setting and a plausible feeder continuation, but the small, generalized municipal map does not securely distinguish the complete chosen westward opening and its early joining arms. Purificación is not transferred to this eastern selection, and the absence of an upper name is not itself the correspondence gap.

correspondence.component_scope: State-boundary approach and El Mezquital reach
correspondence.finding: Mulegé’s Relieve map directly labels the southward watercourse El Mezquital. The selected corridor follows this mountain-front drainage from the state-boundary vicinity toward its southwestward transition. The map distinguishes the more westerly parallel desert washes and the separate channels to the east. Geographic correspondence for this named middle reach is supported at ordinary corridor scale; no exact name-transition point is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: El Mezquital and separate San Pablo junction
correspondence.finding: The municipal map shows El Mezquital descending from the north and the separate San Pablo drainage approaching from the southeast, with the receiving watercourse turning west toward the plain. This supports the meaningful selected connection and distinguishes the chosen northern branch from San Pablo’s headwaters. La Cueva is a separate nearby labeled channel and is not assigned as a whole-system name.

correspondence.component_scope: San José lower plain corridor
correspondence.finding: The municipal map directly labels San José along the long westward plain watercourse. Its connected descent from the mountain-front junction and the broad lower westward course correspond to the selected mainstem. This is distinct from San José de Castro west of the lagoon complex and from the distant San Ignacio river, whose upper Mezquital name is discussed in the 1996 study. The earlier hydrological figure labels a generalized westward desert corridor San Pablo; that older, broader scope is not treated as proof that every selected reach shares one name.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual final plain-to-lagoon connection
correspondence.finding: After the western plain reach, the actual stored path makes a straight northwestward extension to the lagoon-side endpoint. The municipal original instead depicts San José curving farther west and north before approaching another part of the lagoon margin. The 1996 hydrological figure shows the generalized receiving desert corridor ending inland and does not supply the missing selected connection. The distinction concerns an intervening plain-to-lagoon route, not exact banks, a tiny vertex displacement, present flow or reservoir operation. No acquired primary source establishes the actual selected final through-link.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual stored lagoon-side terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The actual last endpoint is in the southeastern lagoon-margin setting identified as Laguna Ojo de Liebre by the municipal hydrography table and the hydrological-study figure. This regional endpoint setting is supported independently of the unproved final connection. It is not the open-Pacific outlet of the lagoon, an official surveyed river mouth or the earlier inland end of the selected plain reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Arid corridor and waterbody context
correspondence.finding: The acquired municipal and hydrological maps show an arid arroyo/plain corridor and a coastal lagoon setting. They show no named reservoir or glacier passage along the selected inland corridor. Regional hydrography prose describes intermittent drainage, but neither that regional description nor lagoon proximity proves continuous surface flow, current saltworks connections, tidal direction or the selected terminal link. No lake name is used as a uniform river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern opening and northwestern headward course
correspondence.finding: Figure35.2 covers the headward vicinity and depicts several unlabelled waterbodies. It does not show a usable continuous connection following the selected opening and northwestern course. Proximity to the Dewar Lakes study area does not identify this feeder or justify a Dewar Lakes name.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper westward passage and southwestern turn
correspondence.finding: The selected upper westward passage and southwestern turn approach and cross the western edge of Figure35.2. The read map does not establish their through-links or distinguish a channel/lake passage throughout this interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle southward course and all successive joins
correspondence.finding: These selected parts lie west of the detailed Tippett field-map footprint. The small regional Figure35.1 is too general to establish the channels, intervening waterbodies or successive connections. No original source resolves this middle interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower westward sweep
correspondence.finding: No usable original mapping was obtained for this long westward sequence or its lake/channel transitions. Regional location or an outlet name alone cannot establish these selected links.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower eastward return and southwestern join
correspondence.finding: The distinctive selected eastward return and subsequent southwestern continuation remain without independent source correspondence. No cross-connection, natural channel or alternative route is inferred from the modeled line.

correspondence.component_scope: Final southwestern course and actual stored terminal
correspondence.finding: The stored sea-class terminal is only selected-model metadata. Flood Brook and Wordie Bay surfaced as lower-end discovery leads, but no permitted original map or field prose was read that establishes this final selected course, its mouth, or its relation to the longer northern sequence. The source and rendered terminal are not silently conflated.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen headward opening east of González Ortega through La Trinidad
correspondence.finding: The Puebla original depicts intermittent drainage in the selected upland valley east/southeast of González Ortega, descending south through the La Trinidad setting toward Rafael J. García. The opening is a short upper tributary corridor, not the source of every river called Huitzilapan. Nearby eastern disappearing streams and western plateau drainages are distinguished from this selected valley. The small line/road offsets are treated at the printed regional scale; no exact vertex or present perennial-flow assertion is made.

correspondence.component_scope: Rafael J. García joining valley and Quimixtlán approach
correspondence.finding: The selected southern turn and eastward joining valley at Rafael J. García continue past the north side of Francisco I. Madero, then northeast toward Quimixtlán. The Puebla map depicts the receiving river and its west/south tributary approaches separately. The selection follows the northern/eastern continuation rather than the southbound drainage toward Rincón de los Reyes. The chosen upper tributary name remains unverified.

correspondence.component_scope: Quimixtlán to Barranca Grande
correspondence.finding: Overlapping Puebla and Veracruz map coverage follows the northeast valley into Barranca Grande, then the east/southeast departure along the south of the Cosautlán de Carvajal setting. Cuanalo identifies the local river as Huitzilapan and reports its junction with the Ixhuacán west of Barranca Grande. This supports the local named component, not an inferred scalar name for the opening tributary.

correspondence.component_scope: Cosautlán/Rincón de Poxtla bend to the northern joining river
correspondence.finding: The mapped selected river makes its southern bend near Rincón de Poxtla and then turns northeast beside the Tlaltetela setting toward the Llano Grande joining area. The southern river coming through the Chichiquila/Totutla setting and the northern river approaching from the Teocelo/San Marcos de León area are separately depicted and their joins are accounted for. Their unselected headwaters are not part of this feature.

correspondence.component_scope: Jalcomulco–Apazapan named central course
correspondence.finding: The Veracruz original follows the selected southeast turn through Jalcomulco, the eastward Apazapan reach and the subsequent bends toward El Carrizal. It prints R. Los Pescados directly along the selected central river. The southern drainage by Santa María Tatetla remains a distinct approaching tributary; the selection does not follow that tributary upstream.

correspondence.component_scope: El Carrizal and Puente Nacional to Cabezas/José Cardel
correspondence.finding: The selected mainstem continues through the El Carrizal bends and Puente Nacional, then east/northeast into the Cabezas–José Cardel setting. Its continuous mapped river corridor and joining approaches are visible. Cuanalo describes the downstream continuation from Los Pescados, after the Santa María contribution, as La Antigua. Exact name-transition points are not asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower turn at La Antigua and actual Gulf terminal
correspondence.finding: The Veracruz original depicts the selected turn south/east from the José Cardel area past La Antigua and the direct river opening into the Gulf of Mexico. The lower southern tributary approaches are distinguished from the selected channel. Both stored terminal parts, including the final coastal crossing, are covered at ordinary generalized scale. No lagoon passage or reservoir transfer is substituted for the terminal.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening and initial westward feeder
correspondence.finding: The selected line begins south/southwest of the Sylvia Grinnell lake region and turns west, then north. The regional satellite overview does not resolve its initial waterbody and each selected feeder/turn. Independent readable corridor mapping of the chosen initial waterbody, westward transfer and first northward join is missing.

correspondence.component_scope: Long northern loop and return toward the lake region
correspondence.finding: The full stored northern loop was considered. The inspected source provides regional terrain and watershed context, but no complete, readable selected lake/river chain through this interval. Each lake entry/exit and the join from the northernmost bend to the southeastern return remain unestablished; a shared watershed outline alone is insufficient.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern lake corridor and Sylvia Grinnell outlet vicinity
correspondence.finding: The regional lake configuration and outlet vicinity correspond to the independently labelled Sylvia Grinnell Lake and Sylvia Grinnell River. The field sketch shows the lake’s southeastern outlet continuing along its own river; the municipal watershed map supplies matching regional context. The full selected western-to-eastern lake passage and all short joins are not established by the schematic field map and overview imagery at their readable scope.
correspondence.candidate_name: Sylvia Grinnell Lake / Sylvia Grinnell River

correspondence.component_scope: Selected southward transfer from the Sylvia Grinnell corridor to the Jordan corridor
correspondence.finding: The stored route turns south after approaching the Sylvia Grinnell outlet region. Macauley Figure 4 depicts Sylvia Grinnell River and the separate upper Jordan River/lake chain without the selected connecting watercourse between them. A mapped through-link for this actual selected transfer is missing. Neither nearby labels nor a regional basin polygon establishes it. This is a geographic material gap, not merely uncertainty over one whole-system name.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper and lower Jordan River corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected southeastern and southern corridor lies in the independently named Jordan River setting. The field report describes a lake/swamp bend and depicts Jordan River running south toward Frobisher Bay; satellite context shows the separate coastal drainage west of Sylvia Grinnell. The schematic report does not distinguish all selected lower river/lake passages and intermediate joins. Continuous selected-corridor correspondence remains incomplete.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual stored terminal and coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The actual stored ending was retained for comparison. It is in the western head-of-Frobisher-Bay coastal setting where Macauley’s field sketch depicts Jordan River entering the sea beside Silliman’s Fossil Mount. This supports regional terminal identity and is not replaced with the Sylvia Grinnell mouth near Iqaluit. The coarse field sketch and broad satellite overview do not establish the complete final selected approach and ending relative to the river/coastal passage. No exact-bank requirement is imposed; ordinary continuous corridor evidence is still missing.
